rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Islam is the greatest blessing, Satan its enemy; preserve it and other blessings, guarding against forgetfulness, hard-heartedness, and ingratitude.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : وأجل النعم على العبد نعمة الإسلام وعدوها إبليس ، فاحفظ هذه النعمة وسائر النعم واحذر من النسيان والقسوة والكفران

rows.speaker: الحسين النوري
rows.claim: Al-Nuri says hardness of heart amid blessings is worse than in hardship: blessing induces complacency, while hardship recalls God.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين النوري رحمه الله : قسوة القلب بالنعم أشد من قسوته بالشدة ، فإنه بالنعمة يسكن وبالشدة يذكر

rows.speaker: الحسين النوري
rows.claim: Al-Nuri warns that indulging in a permitted thing for pleasure wastes life, hardens the heart, and prevents attaining the ranks of the open-hearted.
rows.anchor: وقال : من هم بشيء مما أباحه العلم تلذذا عوقت بتضييع العمر وقسوة القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's beauty, order, and meanings are inexhaustible; it surpasses all earlier prophetic revelations in completeness and firmness.
rows.anchor: هو القرآن الكريم الذي لا نهاية لحسنه ولا غاية لجمال نظمه وملاحة معانيه ، وهو أحسن مما نزل على جميع الأنبياء والمرسلين وأكمله وأكثره إحكاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is the best speech also because of its eloquence and inimitability.
rows.anchor: وأيضا : أحسن الحديث لفصاحته وإعجازه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is best because it is God's eternal speech, whereas the speech of others is created and originated.
rows.anchor: وأيضا : لأنه كلام الله ، وهو قديم وكلام غيره مخلوق محدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is best speech because it is wholly true.
rows.anchor: وأيضا : لكونه صدقا كله إلى غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called hadith because the Prophet told it to his people as revelation came; the common term means report or speech and does not imply that the Quran is originated.
rows.anchor: سمي حديثا ؛ لأن النبي عليه السلام كان يحدث به قومه ويخبرهم بما ينزل عليه منه ، فلا يدل على حدوث القرآن

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines hadith as any speech a person receives by hearing or revelation, while awake or asleep.
rows.anchor: قال في "المفردات" كل كلام يبلغ الإنسان من جهة السمع

rows.speaker: أصحاب رسول الله
rows.claim: The Companions wearied and asked the Prophet to tell them something; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ملوا ملة ، فقالوا له عليه السلام : حدثنا حديثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran offers ample sufficiency in place of other narratives.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أن فيه مندوحة عن سائر الأحاديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتابا is an appositive explaining أحسن الحديث.
rows.anchor: {كتابا} بدل من أحسن الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's contents agree in soundness, rulings, truth, and benefit in both lives; its eloquent words and inimitable structure also correspond.
rows.anchor: معانيه في الصحة والأحكام والابتناء على الحق والصدق واستتباع منافع الخلق في المعاد والمعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثاني is another adjective for the singular كتاب, pluralized in view of the book's parts, as one speaks of Quranic suras and verses or human veins and bones.
rows.anchor: {مثاني} صفة أخرى لكتابا ووصف الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one derivation مثاني means repeated: the Quran repeats its stories, reports, rulings, commands, prohibitions, promises, threats, and exhortations.
rows.anchor: بمعنى مردد ومكرر لما ثنى من قصصه وأنبائه وأحكامه وأوامره ونواهيه ووعده ووعيده ومواعظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean that recitation is repeated without becoming tiresome: its freshness and pleasure remain unlike created speech.
rows.anchor: أو لأنه ثنى في التلاوة ، فلا يمل كما جاء في نعته لا يخلق على كثرة الترداد

rows.speaker: القصيدة البردية
rows.claim: The Burda poem says the Quran's wonders cannot be counted and frequent recitation never makes it tiresome.
rows.anchor: فلا تعد ولا تحصى عجائبها ولا تسام على الإكثار بالسأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat explains that suras are called mathani because they recur over time and do not fade away like other things, though paper wears out.
rows.anchor: وفي "المفردات" وسمي سور القرآن مثاني ؛ لأنها تثنى على مرور الأيام وتكرر

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: The author cites a report that Uthman burned two mushafs because of how frequently he read them.
rows.anchor: كما روي أن عثمان رضي الله عنه حرق مصحفين لكثرة قراءته فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can be called mathani because its benefits renew continually, and its wonders never run out.
rows.anchor: ويصح أن يقال للقرآن : مثاني لما يثنى ويتجدد حالا فحالا من فوائده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation makes mathani praise: the Quran continually gives grounds for praise, as reflected in its descriptions as noble and glorious.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذلك من الثناء تنبيها على أنه أبدا يظهر منه ما يدعو إلى الثناء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathani may also derive from repetition or return, as in a gaze returned twice, meaning one turn after another.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى : {ثم ارجع البصر كرتين}

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some derive it as something praised for eloquence and inimitability, so that a listener might say one should prostrate for its eloquence.
rows.anchor: حتى قال بعضهم لبعض : ألا سجدت لفصاحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the final n pronounced kasra, مثني عليه means praised for the attributes worthy of it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بكسر النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause resumes by describing the Quran's visible effects on listeners after its qualities and status as the best speech were explained.
rows.anchor: {تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم} ، استئناف مسوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicons explain اقشعر as a shiver or tremor; the skin is the body's outer covering, and the root suggests trembling or strong contraction from sudden fear.
rows.anchor: والجلد : قشر البدن كما في "المفردات"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Irshad describes the skin as contracting intensely and says the form adds an intensified sense of sudden fear that raises the hair.
rows.anchor: وفي "الإرشاد" : الاقشعرار التقبض يقال : اقشعر الجلد إذا تقبض تقبضا شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may depict extreme fear figuratively or report an actual bodily state; Bursevi prefers the literal reading because fear's bodily effect is directly felt.
rows.anchor: والمراد : إما بيان إفراط خشيتهم بطريق التمثيل والتصوير أو بيان حصول تلك الحالة وعروضها لهم بطريق التحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they hear the Quran's threatening verses, awe and fear make their skins shiver and bristle.
rows.anchor: إذا سمعوا بالقرآن وقوارع آيات وعيده أصابتهم هيبة وخشية تقشعر منها جلودهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Softness, opposite of roughness, is literal for bodies and metaphorical for character; skins signify bodies and hearts signify souls, which soften upon recalling God's mercy and forgiveness as fear becomes hope.
rows.anchor: والجلود عبارة عن الأبدان والقلوب عن النفوس كما في "المفردات" ؛ أي : ثم إذا ذكروا رحمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is followed by إلى because softness includes the sense of settling and becoming tranquil toward God's remembrance, in a hopeful and uncontracted state.
rows.anchor: وتعدية اللين بإلى لتضمنه معنى السكون والاطمئنان ؛ كأنه قيل : تسكن وتطمئن إلى ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says God's remembrance without naming mercy because mercy is the first thing that comes to mind when He is remembered.
rows.anchor: وإنما أطلق ذكر الله ولم يصرح بالرحمة إيذانا بأنها أول ما يخطر بالبال عند ذكره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Skin is named first because fear first affects the heart: warning makes skins bristle and hearts fear, then hope replaces fear in the heart and softens the skin.
rows.anchor: لتقدم الخشية التي هي من عوارض القلوب ، فكأنه قيل : تقشعر جلودهم من آيات الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses signify fear and hope, contraction and expansion, awe and intimacy, or manifestation and concealment.
rows.anchor: فالجملتان إشارة إلى الخوف والرجاء أو القبض والبسط أو الهيبة والأنس

rows.speaker: النهرجوري
rows.claim: Al-Nahrjurī says the verse describes the audition of seekers and knowers: the seekers manifest a state, while knowers attain calm; shivering marks beginners and softness the advanced.
rows.anchor: قال النهرجوري رحمه الله : وصف الله بهذه الآية سماع المريدين وسماع العارفين

rows.speaker: أم الدرداء
rows.claim: Shahr ibn Hawshab reports Umm al-Darda saying that heart-fear resembles a burning palm frond; when gooseflesh appears, pray, for the heart is drawn to the sacred realm and intimacy, and prayer then is answered.
rows.anchor: وعن شهر بن حوشب قالت أم الدرداء : رضي الله عنها : إنما الوجل في قلب الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book just described is God's guidance; He guides believing, God-fearing people who reflect on its hidden signs and proofs of its divine origin, as in 2:2.
rows.anchor: الكتاب الذي شرح أحواله

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes misguidance by creating it in a person who turns from guidance and remains unaffected by warning or promise; no guide can rescue that person from error.
rows.anchor: أي : يخلق فيه الضلالة لصرف قدرته إلى مباديها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says God misguides one by leaving him to himself and his intellect and depriving him of faith in, and following, the prophets.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {ومن يضلل الله} بأن يكله إلى نفسه وعقله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says no guide from philosophers' proofs or rational arguments can guide such a person.
rows.anchor: من براهين الفلاسفة والدلائل العقلية

rows.speaker: أحد الصحابة
rows.claim: A Companion asks why believers' faces redden when hearing Quran while hypocrites' faces blacken; the answer is that Quran lights believers and burns hypocrites.
rows.anchor: (يكى ازصحابه روزى بآن مهتر عالم عليه السلام كفت يا رسول الله جرا رخساره ما در استماع قرآن

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Al-Jami counsels that whoever seeks the Kaaba of realization should not wander the path without a guide.
rows.anchor: قال المولى الجامي قدس سره : خواهى بصوب كعبه تحقيق ره برى

rows.speaker: الخجندي
rows.claim: Al-Khujandi's verse contrasts hearts that receive Quran continually with false people who tire of God's speech.
rows.anchor: قال الخجندي قدس سره :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated Quranic admonition softens resistant souls, which naturally recoil from counsel; the Prophet repeated his exhortations three or seven times.
rows.anchor: لأن النفوس أنفر شيء من حديث الوعظ والنصيحة وأكثر جمودا وإباء عنه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says that when a servant's skin shivers from fear of God, his sins fall away like leaves from a dry tree.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله تحاتت عنه ذنوبه"

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another report from the Prophet says God forbids the Fire to a servant whose skin shivers from fear of Him.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام : "إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله حرمه الله على النار"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God made Abraham His intimate friend, He placed such fear in his heart that its beating could be heard from afar, like a bird's flutter in the air.
rows.anchor: ولما اتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا ألقى في قلبه الوجل حتى إن خفقان قلبه يسمع من بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza is interrogative denial, the fa connects to an omitted proposition, and the conditional has an omitted predicate: are people equal, when the unbeliever must shield himself with his face, his noblest limb?
rows.anchor: الهمزة : للإنكار والفاء : للعطف على محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اتقى بكذا means making something a shield against what harms oneself; here the unbeliever uses his face as a shield.
rows.anchor: يقال : اتقى فلان بكذا إذا جعله وقاية لنفسه والتركيب يدل على دفع شيء عن شيء يضره

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi's Persian commentary glosses the evil punishment as the flame of fire.
rows.anchor: يعني (زبانه آتش) ، كما في "تفسير الفارسي" للكاشفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day the unbeliever's hands are shackled to his neck, unlike the safe believer, so he must ward off punishment with his face.
rows.anchor: لكون يده التي بها كان يتقي المكاره والمخاوف مغلولة إلى عنقه كمن هو آمن

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya reads it as turning one's face toward the evil punishment to fend it off, unlike one who does not protect himself and wrongs himself.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {أفمن يتقى بوجهه} توجه {وجهه} {سواء العذاب}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are those who substituted disbelief for faith, denial for affirmation, and disobedience for obedience; the command is spoken by the keepers of Hell.
rows.anchor: الذين وضعوا الكفر موضع الإيمان والتكذيب موضع التصديق والعصيان موضع الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense wording signals certainty; naming them explicitly as wrongdoers records their guilt and explains the order to taste punishment.
rows.anchor: وصيغة الماضي للدلالة على التحقيق ووضع المظهر في مقام المضمر للتسجيل عليهم بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their recompense is what they continually earned in worldly life through disbelief, denial, and sins.
rows.anchor: وبال ما كنتم تكسبونه في الدنيا على الدوام من الكفر والتكذيب والمعاصي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says they had been within punishment through vile acts and traits but did not taste it while asleep in heedlessness; death awakened them to it.
rows.anchor: بأفعالكم الرديئة وأخلاقكم الدنيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier nations denied their prophets just as Muhammad's people denied him, and each received its appointed punishment unexpectedly while secure and unaware.
rows.anchor: كذبوا أنبياءهم كما كذبك قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that the punished people could not identify any means of repelling or averting the punishment.
rows.anchor: لا يعرفون له مدفعا ولا مردا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says punishment came disguised as health, blessing, and joy, without their realizing it was punishment; the worst punishment is unexpected.
rows.anchor: أتاهم العذاب في صورة الصحة والنعمة والسرور وهم لا يشعرون أنه العذاب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines kaffara as covering sin; takfir covers it until it is as though the deed had never been done.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الكفارة ما يغطي الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takfir can also mean removing disbelief or ingratitude, by analogy with tamrid meaning removal of illness.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى إزالة الكفر والكفران كالتمريض

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar offers two attachments for the lām: to المحسنين, who acted well hoping for forgiveness, or to the reward, given so God might cover their worst deeds.
rows.anchor: واللام متصل بالمحسنين ، يعني الذين أحسنوا رجاء أن يكفر الله

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abu al-Su'ud attaches the lām to لهم ما يشاؤون understood as a promise: God promises to remove their harms and grant joys, thereby covering their worst deeds.
rows.anchor: اللام متعلق بقوله : لهم ما يشاؤون

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: In an anecdote, David explains that he eats a morsel without knowing whether it is lawful or unlawful, expressing scrupulous concern about its source.
rows.anchor: هذه الكسرة آكلها ولا أدري أمن حلال هي أم من حرام

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد أبو الخير
rows.claim: Asked what truth is and how to reach God, Abu Sa'id says truth is God's trust in His servants, in which the lower self has no share; the self cannot reach the Real.
rows.anchor: (وشيخ أبو سعيد أبو الخير قدس سره را در مجلس سؤال كردندكه).

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Muadh to purify his religion, for a little deed will then suffice him.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام لمعاذ رضي الله عنه : "يا معاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza over negation affirms and establishes God's sufficiency; sufficiency fills need and achieves the desired end.
rows.anchor: أدخلت همزة الإنكار على كلمة النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God suffices Muhammad against his enemies and supports him against them, consoling him; the wording may encompass everyone who realizes true servitude.
rows.anchor: هو تعالى كاف عبده محمدا صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أمر من يعاديه

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some great Sufis read the servant as one who worships God and believes in Him, or one realizing the divine identity from which divinity begins.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض الكبار أليس بكاف عبده

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says God suffices His servant against everything, while nothing can suffice the servant against God; even the treasures of the heavens do not divert the Prophet from beholding God.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : أن الله كافف عبده عن كل شيء

rows.speaker: عرائس البقلي
rows.claim: The Arā'is al-Baqli sees a gentle reproach: God asks whether servants imagine He will abandon His care and protection; no one dares oppose one under His eternal regard.
rows.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلي" : فيه نبذة من

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says whoever abandons choice and scheming, returns sincerely to God in every state, and seeks help only from Him will be sheltered by divine acceptance and freed from all concerns.
rows.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" : من تبرأ من اختياره واحتياله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says God suffices the worldly and afterlife concerns of one who wakes with a single concern.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من أصبح وهمومه هم واحد

rows.speaker: عبد الواحد زيد
rows.claim: Abd al-Wahid Zayd predicts that Utba al-Ghulam, absorbed in watching the Creator, will enter; when asked, Utba says he saw no one although his route was the crowded marketplace.
rows.anchor: (عبد الواحد زيدرا كفتند هيج كس را دانى كه در مراقبت خالق جنان مستغرق

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Ja'far al-Sadiq says no beauty exceeds the rich person's humility toward the poor, except the poor person's disregard of the rich through sufficiency in God and His care.
rows.anchor: وقال السيد جعفر الصادق رضي الله عنه : ما رأيت أحسن من تواضع الأغنياء للفقراء

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says anyone not satisfied with his Lord's sufficiency after this verse belongs among the doomed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر رحمه الله : من لم يكف بربه

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says that after this verse, looking to, hoping in, fearing, or coveting anything among creatures strips away the marks of servitude.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : رفع جلاجل العبودية من عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists frighten Muhammad with their idols, claiming that because he insults them they will kill, madden, or physically harm him.
rows.anchor: أي : المشركون {بالذين من دونه} ؛ أي : بالأوثان

rows.speaker: بعض أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Some exegetes say the verse was revealed once about the Prophet and again about Khalid ibn al-Walid, just as al-Fatiha was revealed in Mecca and Medina.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل التفسير : إن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: خالد بن الوليد
rows.claim: A report says Arab idolaters worshipped a tree with a demon called al-Uzza beneath it; sent to uproot it, Khalid ignored their threats, killed the demon, and the Prophet declared al-Uzza would never be worshipped again.
rows.anchor: ونزولش در حق خالد بن الوليد آنست كه قومى از مشركان عرب درختى را

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God misguides one from the straight way and sound understanding so that he forgets God's sufficiency and protection and fears what cannot harm or benefit.
rows.anchor: ومن يجعله دالا عن الطريق القويم والفهم المستقيم حتى غفل عن كفايته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No guide remains to direct the person to what is good.
rows.anchor: فما له من هاد} يهديه إلى خير ما

words: وَمَن يَهْدِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّضِلٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever God guides to the straight path cannot be diverted from his destination or harmed in a way that disrupts his course, since no one can repel God's act or oppose His will.
rows.anchor: أي : ومن يرشده إلى الصراط المستقيم

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya says seeing good or evil as coming from other than God is misguidance, and the true guide or misleader is God, whom none can countermand.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : فيه إشارة إلى أن رؤية الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is invincible and prevailing, granting honor to those who worship Him; He takes vengeance on His enemies for His allies.
rows.anchor: غالب منيع يعز من يعبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As previously, an interrogative over negation establishes and confirms the assertion.
rows.anchor: لأن الاستفهام إذا دخل على النفي أفاد تحقيقا وتقريرا كما مر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian gloss gives intiqam as vengeance; Bahr al-Ulum relates it to punishment and severity.
rows.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" : من النقمة ، وهي الشدة والعقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes what most people do rather than every human being without exception.
rows.anchor: إخبار عن الجنس بما يفعله غالب أفراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa orders this response after the preceding description: polytheists recoil from God's mention alone but rejoice at idols, yet appeal to God when hardship strikes.
rows.anchor: والفاء : لترتيب ما بعدها على ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reversal makes disbelief the means of turning to God in place of faith, though faith should be the means of seeking Him.
rows.anchor: حيث جعلوا الكفر سببا في الالتجاء إلى الله بأن أقاموه مقام الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwalnah means giving a blessing as a favor; it is not used for a recompense.
rows.anchor: أعطيناه إياها تفضلا ، فإن التخويل مختص بما كان بطريق التفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of “upon knowledge” is that the person knows the means by which the blessing was acquired.
rows.anchor: على علم مني بوجوه كسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading is that the person knew he would receive the blessing because of his merit and deserving.
rows.anchor: أو بأني سأعطاه لما لي من الفضل والاستحقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading is that God knew the person deserved the blessing.
rows.anchor: أو على علم من الله باستحقاقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the relative expression أن الذي أوتيته or to the blessing if the particle إن is taken as redundant; masculine form represents a thing or portion of a blessing.
rows.anchor: بمعنى أن الذي أوتيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rejects the claim: the blessing is instead a trial testing whether the person gives thanks or disbelieves, like gold tested in fire for its quality.
rows.anchor: أي : محنة وابتلاء له أيشكر أم يكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people do not know that a bestowed blessing is a test and a gradual enticement.
rows.anchor: أن التخويل استدراج وامتحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in قالها refers to that utterance, namely the claim “I was given it on account of knowledge.”
rows.anchor: وهي قوله : {إنما أوتيته على علم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi identifies Qarun and his people: Qarun claimed knowledge of his own worth, and his people approved his claim, so both are included.
rows.anchor: وهم قارون وقومه حيث قال : إنما أوتيته على علم عندي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some allow that the phrase includes any earlier people, good or evil, who became arrogant and deceived by outward prosperity, not Qarun alone.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : يجوز أن يكون جميع من تقدمنا من الخيار والشرار

words: فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly possessions did not avert punishment or torment and were of no use to them.
rows.anchor: أن النعمة لم تدفع عنهم النقمة والعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Al-Mufradat that aghna anhu means to suffice or be enough for someone.
rows.anchor: إذا كفاه كما في "المفردات"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are driven with their leader in successive groups; zumar is a plural of zumra, a small group, and derives from zamr, sound made by a gathering.
rows.anchor: مع إمامهم حال كونهم {زمرا} : جماعة جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian gloss of سوق is driving; they are driven after the reckoning by God's simple command.
rows.anchor: (راندن) ؛ أي : سيقوا إليها بعد إقامة الحساب بأمر يسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are driven harshly and in humiliation in separate waves ordered according to degrees of error and wickedness; Hell scowls at them as they scowled at commands and their bearers.
rows.anchor: وذلك بالعنف والإهانة حال كونهم أفواجا متفرقة بعضها في إثر بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى introduces a narrative clause after the preceding sentence, and the answer to إذا is فتحت أبوابها.
rows.anchor: وجواب إذا قوله : {فتحت أبوابها} السبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They arrive at Hell in humiliation and disgrace.
rows.anchor: (تاجون بيايند بدوزخ بر صفت دلت وخوارى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell has seven gates, as stated in 15:44; leaving them closed until the disbelievers arrive heightens its horror and heat.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : {لها سبعة أبواب}

rows.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
rows.claim: As'ilat al-Hikam says the gates are closed like prison doors, forcing the people of Hell to wait for them to open as humiliation and rebuke.
rows.anchor: قال في "أسئلة الحكم" : أهل النار يجدونها مغلقة الأبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi calls the wait at the gates spiritual punishment, worse than bodily pain; prolonged standing in terror can make an unbeliever beg God for relief even by means of the Fire.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : هذا من قبيل العذاب الروحاني ، وهو أشد من العذاب الجسماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven gates signify seven blameworthy traits—pride, stinginess, greed, lust, envy, anger, and rancor; everyone entering Hell passes through one, so the soul must be purified of them.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى الأوصاف الذميمة النفسانية السبعة : وهي الكبر والبخل والحرص والشهوة والحسد والغضب والحقد
